title: Feedback rules only its own course
statement: Treat feedback on one course as a ruling for that course only, and check each point against another course's build before carrying it over.
example: Four complaints about a Grade 3 build did not apply to the Grade 5 build, which already handled them, while one more, a passive modelling phase, did.
detail: A reading-lesson project's standing rules scope feedback to the course it was given on and say that a matching string in another course is not a ruling. When feedback raised on a Grade 3 build was checked against the Grade 5 build, four complaints (sentence starters, feedback that restates instead of evaluating, minimum-word limits that force padding, and telling the student what to type) did not apply, because the Grade 5 build already handled them. A fifth, that the modelling phase gives the student nothing to do, did carry over.
against: The record close-the-class-not-the-instance asks for a defect to be repaired wherever content was made the same way, so a point that does apply to another course still has to be carried over there. The wiki page used here summarises a fuller record kept in another repository.

evidence.quote: **Reviewer feedback is scoped to its own course.** A matching string elsewhere is not a ruling.
**5. The 'I do' is passive — transfers from G3 to G5**
